description.narrative: On 19 November 2025, the County Commissioner of Leer, representing the Unity State Government, formally acknowledged the severity of the ongoing flooding crisis and appealed for urgent humanitarian assistance to support 8,804 households (63,657 individuals). The floods have displaced families and destroyed critical infrastructure, leaving communities with acute needs across multiple sectors. Immediate priorities include food assistance and agricultural recovery inputs to restore livelihoods disrupted by floodwaters, Safe shelter and non-food items (NFIs) to protect households exposed to harsh conditions, strengthened WASH services to prevent outbreaks of cholera, diarrhea, hepatitis E, malaria, and snakebites, targeted protection measures for women, the elderly, and persons with disabilities and health and nutrition support for malnourished children and pregnant women, given the damage to health facilities. While national assessments have highlighted the broader impact of flooding across Unity State, localized vulnerabilities in Leer remain under documented. Without rapid, flexible funding, these gaps will persist, leaving communities at heightened risk of disease outbreaks, deepening food insecurity, and further displacement as the crisis evolves.
